dedupe_keys.name: topology bench real and synthetic core optical network topologies

description: Topology Bench is a dataset of core optical network topologies built for benchmarking studies, from the Optical Networks Group at University College London. It holds 105 georeferenced real-world core optical networks, which the authors say increases the number of spatially referenced real networks available by 61.5 per cent, and 270,900 validated synthetic topologies, plus a smaller subset of 900, all in a common format that gives node locations and the links connecting cities. The accompanying paper analyses real and synthetic networks with structural, spatial and spectral graph metrics, clusters the real networks with k-means on nine selected metrics, and gives guidance on choosing a diverse set of topologies for studies instead of picking them by habit or availability. Coverage: national and continental core networks worldwide. Format and access: zip files of CSV and graph data on Zenodo (about 3.3 GB), with analysis code on GitHub; free under CC BY 4.0. Caveats: real networks are compiled from public maps and papers, so link capacities and exact routes are not included; synthetic graphs are generated, not measured. Simulation uses: benchmark topologies for routing, capacity planning and failure studies, and testing resilience methods across many network shapes. Related records: the Internet Topology Zoo and SNDlib are older topology collections, and GNPy models optical links.
